They can work on schedules or app events, create their own triggers, and spin up lightweight apps and dashboards. Every run is durable, observable, and available for your team to inspect.  
  
Teams can chat with agents in Keystroke, use them in Slack or Teams, run workflows, manage credentials, share context and skills, and collaborate from one shared workspace. Under the hood, everything teams build is ordinary TypeScript. You can keep it in git, grep it, test it, review it, and run it anywhere. [...] Hey Product Hunt 👋  
  
I’m Blake, cofounder of Keystroke.  
  
We built Keystroke because creating an agent is only one small part of putting it to work inside a company.  
  
You also need integrations, credentials, memory, workflows, triggers, approvals, observability, and a place where your team can actually use and improve what you build. Today, those pieces are usually scattered across agent frameworks, scripts, infrastructure, and automation tools.  
  
Keystroke brings all these things together in one collaborative platform.  
  
Describe the agent or AI system you need directly inside Keystroke, and the built-in agent builds it, connects your tools, runs tests, and deploys it to your workspace. You can also build with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any coding agent.

### Why we picked it

Gumloop is an experimentation layer. Reviews describe chaining prompts, building agents, testing workflows, and prototyping internal tools. AI is the foundation, not a feature—reviewers connect it to ChatGPT, Gemini, and other models to push what's possible in low-code environments.

> The product is incredible, both with its flexibility and power. Building with drag and drop feels like lego, but this is not a toy. You can build useful and dynamic utility with AI that connects to your favourite data sources, and further extend with web hooks as triggers - and once it works once, you can depend on it to scale.

### Pros - Best use cases

Builders who want to chain prompts, test AI workflows, and iterate fast without production overhead. [...] Human checkpoints are treated as features, not compromises. Several reviews describe using Relay's AI agents for operational decision-making—routing edge cases, approving sensitive requests, and managing processes that can't just fire and forget. Relay makes workflows explainable to the people accountable for their outcomes.

> The value proposition is unbeatable. I was able to build a custom replacement for a specialized SaaS tool that was costing us double what we now pay for our entire Relay.app subscription. With just a Google Form, a single AI agent, and a few workflows, we replaced a manual intake process. It now runs in real time and handles edge cases automatically.
